title: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council: The Amelia Scott, Collecting Tomorrow
summary: The Amelia Scott reports 50% faster image processing, improved scans, interactive exhibits, and volunteers progressing to paid museum roles.
account: The Amelia Scott uses Adobe Lightroom AI in artifact-imaging workflows, producing digital twins and tactile display objects. The council reports 50% faster scan/image processing and better scan quality, plus actual interactive exhibitions and digital/physical-twin outputs. Potential commercial revenue is not realized income. A richer visitor experience is not equivalent to measured learning gains. Training, partnerships, and digital production jointly contribute to these results. The source does not isolate AI’s contribution to employment or visitor learning.
purpose: Improve artifact-imaging workflows and create digital and tactile museum experiences.
system: Adobe Lightroom generative-AI functions within The Amelia Scott’s 3D scanning and digital-twin workflow
deployer: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council, The Amelia Scott

ratings.reason: Improved digital twins and delivered interactive/tactile exhibits extend the museum’s capabilities. Processing speed alone would be depth 1.
The source reports skill development, volunteers obtaining paid roles, and expanded ways to experience artifacts. These are capability/opportunity gains without established livelihood preservation.

ai_role.statement: The source attributes faster masking, editing, and improved scan preparation to Lightroom AI within a broader production workflow. Training, partnerships, and other tools also contribute, so employment and visitor-learning effects cannot be isolated to AI.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council: The Amelia Scott, Collecting Tomorrow

produced_by: The museum worked with PolyPlay to improve existing 3D-scanning workflows.
Digital twins were used in interactive exhibitions and tactile objects, with volunteers and learners involved in production.
must_hold: The source does not establish which conditions are necessary to reproduce the reported benefit.

headline: The Amelia Scott reports better scans and expanded digital exhibits

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The deployer's report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
